name: Gaius
fiction_note: Gaius is an original fictional commander, not a historical general, actor or imitation of a living person.
future_note: Marcus offers reactive milestone guidance. Lucius joins through completed government development; Gaius through completed barracks development. Their explicit seasonal council and authored Zeus/Ares dilemmas are available now. Campaign memory recalls retained records across rulers and shows its sources; earlier conversations are not saved as history. A larger pantheon remains future story work.

ui.hear_hint: When connected, ask Gaius to explain the current page with speech and text.

ui.connection_note: Connect to send questions and visible campaign facts to ElevenLabs. Replies include text and optional speech. Closing Gaius ends the online session. The written guide and seasonal briefing work offline.
ui.context_note: Counsel uses a snapshot taken when you ask. Check current reports and order previews before acting. Running battles continue while you read.

intro.title: A place at the war table
intro.body: I am Gaius. Before we speak of victory, let us learn what you command, what lies along the road and what the reports cannot tell us. An order spends more than movement: it commits you to a place and a consequence.
intro.counsel: Know what must remain behind before deciding what may go forward.

lesson_counsel: A force is a responsibility before it is an instrument. Count what it can do today.
A familiar road can still hold an unfamiliar danger. Distinguish knowledge of the ground from knowledge of the enemy.
Do not mistake a possible march for a necessary one. Review what its destination would ask of you.
Read the present fight, but leave the command with the player. A snapshot is already becoming the past.
A lesson from the season should change a question before it changes an order.

lessons.title: Know the force you command
lessons.body: Select one of your own armies or fleets to read its strength, upkeep and remaining movement. An owned settlement can also supply a garrison reading. Gaius can interpret these visible facts; he cannot recruit, replenish, split or move troops for you.

lessons.title: Read the ground before the road
lessons.body: A known region exposes its reported terrain, crossing and step cost. Current observation and an older survey are different evidence. Compare the visible route and order preview; do not treat a distant report as proof that a road is clear.

lessons.title: Inspect an order before committing
lessons.body: Review the pinned or queued march: target, cost, timing and any reported block or uncertainty. Show me opens the campaign controls, not an order. Only the game’s existing order controls can commit the march.

lessons.title: Counsel during a city battle
lessons.body: During a viewed battle, Gaius reads only its detached displayed snapshot and selected defending formations. He does not read the live campaign economy or hidden attackers. The advisor never pauses, aims, chooses targets or issues tactical orders. If already in Roma, Show me opens its campaign ledger; enter and control battles through the game’s existing battle controls.

lessons.title: Return to the war table
lessons.body: After the season and Dispatch finish, convene the council. Compare Gaius’s readiness concerns with Marcus’s duties and Lucius’s governing costs. The latest reports are evidence of resolved events, not a promise of future success.
